patch.value: The first pm context --for orient on a fresh clone or worktree rebuilds the whole SQLite history event index on the read path, although orient only needs the latest substantive event of its focus items

Measured 2026-11-20 on a copy of this repository's tracker (3,354 history streams, 135 MB) with runtime/ and search/ removed, as every fresh clone and agent worktree starts: the first pm context --for orient --limit 3 took 20.0 s, the next two 2.0 s and 2.4 s. A CPU profile of the cold run (tsx, 21 s) attributes about 6 s to the history event index (populateHistoryEventIndex 3.8 s with insertEvent 3.7 s, plus readHistorySnapshot of every stream about 2 s) and produces a 214 MB runtime/history-event-index.sqlite; the remaining cold cost is the item metadata cache rebuild (readCachedDocumentParts 5.2 s parsing every TOON item, rebuildItemMetadataQueryIndex 2.0 s, persistCache 0.9 s), which is item-scale and owned by the derived read index work (pm-801d). The trigger is readLatestSubstantiveHistoryEvents in src/core/history/event-index.ts: when the index is missing it calls rebuildHistoryEventIndex(pmRoot, { lockWaitMs: 0 }) for the whole corpus before answering for the few requested focus streams, although its own authoritative per-stream fallback answers those streams by reading only them. Found while bounding the activity section of the same read (pm-gh1664), whose fixture benchmark excludes this first read for the same reason. Duplicate check: searched fresh clone, cold start, event index rebuild, first read and worktree; pm-431035 owns the graph index's per-clone rebuild and pm-801d the item metadata index, neither the history event index.

A read that needs at most a bounded number of streams answers from those streams when the event index is missing, without building the global index on the read path; The global index is built by an explicit reindex, a write path that already maintains it, or a background step whose cost is not charged to the requesting read; A cold pm context --for orient --limit 3 on a fresh copy of a tracker with thousands of streams and more than 100 MB of history spends no time in populateHistoryEventIndex, proven by a spec that counts streams read on the cold path; Output is identical to the warm path
A cold-start orient read on a fresh clone costs time proportional to the streams it needs, not to the history archive
20.0 s for the first orient on a fresh copy of a 135 MB tracker, about 6 s of it rebuilding a 214 MB SQLite event index
